_comment: Every threshold compute_pulse.py and check_experiments.py apply. These are conventions of the stack, chosen so a small site does not read noise as news; they are not industry benchmarks. A project overrides any key with a pulse_rules object in <project>/growth-pulse/config.json. The model never recomputes them.

weeks._comment: ISO weeks, Monday to Sunday. The report week is the last complete week before the run date. The 4-week reference is the mean of the 4 weeks before the report week (previous week included), over the weeks that are complete.

volume._comment: No percentage is computed on fewer than min_events_for_pct events: under 30, one event more or less moves a percentage by more than 3 points. A count change on a smaller base is given in absolute terms; a rate is given as 'x of y'; a revenue change is given in money with the payment count.

noise._comment: A count change is 'flat' when it stays within z standard deviations. The deviation is the larger of two: a Poisson count (difference of two weeks: sqrt(current + previous); against the 4-week mean m over k weeks: sqrt(m x (1 + 1/k))) and the observed spread of the reference weeks (sample standard deviation s: s x sqrt(2) against last week, s x sqrt(1 + 1/k) against the mean), computed when at least min_weeks_for_spread reference weeks are complete. Impressions and pageviews come in bursts and need the second. A rate change uses the two-proportion standard error. An approximation, not a significance test. Average position moves of less than position_flat_band are flat.

correlation._comment: Only the pairs below are tested, fixed in advance so the report never goes fishing across every metric. Pearson r on daily values after removing the day-of-week mean of each series, b shifted by lag days after a. A pair is 'correlated' at |r| >= min_abs_r with at least min_days paired days. A correlation is never a cause: both series may follow a third thing.

pairs.question: Do social impressions and site visitors move together?
Do search clicks and site visitors move together?
Do conversions follow traffic, or move on their own?

gsc_decline._comment: Mirror of the decline object of seo-audit's gsc-bands.json, so both agents call the same thing a decline: clicks down at least 20 % against the prior period with at least 10 prior clicks; cause position when the average position worsened by 2 or more, demand when impressions fell 20 % or more, else ctr; gone when the row disappeared. Here the prior period is the previous week. The selftest fails when the two files drift apart. A project override in <project>/seo-audit/config.json (gsc_bands.decline) is read too, so one override serves both agents.

experiments._comment: check_experiments.py: exactly count experiments, AARRR stages only, duration in days within the bounds, at least min_distinct_stages stages unless config.focus_stage pins one, any cash spend flagged for approval and within config.budget_eur_per_sprint when set.
